app.name: CexChain
nav.label: Main
language.label: Language
sign_in.title: Sign in
sign_in.intro: Use the passkey you registered for this console.
enroll.title: Register your passkey
enroll.intro: This link works once. It registers a passkey on this device for this console.
enroll.name: Your name
enroll.name_hint: 1 to 64 letters, digits, spaces, dots, dashes, or underscores.
home.title: Home
things.title: Things
things.hint: This list comes from the console; a thing's page will check its proof in this browser.
error.title: Something went wrong
error.no_passkeys: This browser cannot use passkeys. Try a recent browser, or another device.
error.cancelled: The passkey was not used. Try again when you are ready.
error.address: Passkeys need this console's name: open it at http://localhost (not an IP address).
keys.locked: This console is locked: it signs nothing until it is unlocked.
keys.secret_hint: A passkey that unlocked the console before unlocks it when you sign in.
keys.wrong: That does not unlock the console.
act.label: Act on this {type} record
act.title: Act on a record
act.role_hint: For example: reviewed, approved. Needed to endorse.
approve.title: Approve with your passkey
approve.intro: This is exactly what will be signed in your name. Nothing is signed until your passkey approves it.
approve.done: Signed and registered on the ledger as entry {index}.
approve.checked_here: Checked in this browser: these are the bytes your passkey signs.
approve.checked_by_console: This console has no check in the browser: what you see is the console's description.
approve.mismatch: The console's answer does not match what it asked you to sign. Nothing was signed.
setup.title: Set up your console
setup.intro: Your name (a nickname works) also names your ledger. Your passkey (Touch ID, Windows Hello, a phone, or a security key) is how you sign in and approve.
sheet.title: Your recovery code
sheet.intro: If you lose your passkey, this code lets you register a new one, and it unlocks the console's keys. Anyone who has it can take over this console: keep it offline, somewhere safe.
sheet.once: The console shows it this once.
sheet.saved: I have printed or saved my recovery code
sheet.needed: Print or save the code first, then tick the box.
backup.title: Where should backups go?
backup.intro: Choose a folder on an external disk, or one that your cloud drive syncs.
backup.folder_hint: A full path. The console makes the folder if it is missing.
recover.title: Recover with your recovery code
recover.intro: Type the code from your recovery sheet, then create a new passkey on this device. The lost passkey stops working.
recover.code_hint: 26 letters and digits; dashes and spaces do not matter.
recover.name: Owner's name (optional)
recover.name_hint: Needed only if this console has more than one owner.
recover.wrong: That is not this console's recovery code.
recover.done: Your new passkey is now the only one. The lost one no longer signs in or approves.
home.locked: The ledger shows here once the console is unlocked.
settings.title: Settings
settings.language_here: This browser's language is chosen at the top of the page.
settings.backup_note: Every day while the console is unlocked, it writes a backup there, sealed so that only your recovery code opens it, and keeps the newest seven and one a week for four weeks. Keep the code apart from the folder.
settings.read_only: Only an owner or an admin changes these.
settings.keys_state.locked: Locked: the console signs nothing until it is unlocked.
slot.intro: Your passkey does not unlock this console yet. Sign in with it once more, and it will unlock the console after a restart.
register.title: Register a document
register.no_kinds: There is no kind of document yet.
register.private_hint: Private: only its commitment is on the ledger, until you disclose it.
register.public_hint: Public: anyone who reads the ledger sees it.
register.files_kept: Kept with the record, sealed; the ledger holds only their commitments. 16 MiB a file at most.
register.files_not_kept: The ledger holds only their commitments: keep the files yourself.
kinds.title: Kinds
kinds.hint: A kind is this console's form for a kind of document: its fields and its files. The ledger keeps the documents, not the forms.
kinds.name: Name
kinds.type_hint: How the ledger names its records. Change it only if you have a reason.
kinds.keep: Keep the files with the record, sealed
thing.private_hidden: Hidden from you: only those allowed see a document's private data.
thing.private_locked: Unlock the console to see them.
thing.private_elsewhere: This console does not hold the document's private data.
thing.not_kept: not kept: its owner has it
share.title: Share proof
share.intro: The proof is a file anyone can check without trusting this console. It shows the document's history; private fields stay hidden unless you disclose them.
share.nothing_private: No private fields can be disclosed from here.
share.files: Let it check the files (send the files along)
share.send: Send the proof file to whoever checks it. They verify it in the Verify screen, in the standalone verifier page, or with cexchain verify.
share.send_files: Send the proof file and the files to whoever checks them. They verify them in the Verify screen, in the standalone verifier page, or with cexchain verify.
verify.link: Check a proof someone sent you
verify.title: Verify a proof
verify.intro: Checked in this browser, with the same verifier as cexchain verify: nothing is sent anywhere.
verify.drop: Drop the proof file here, with the files it covers.
verify.ledger_hint: From whoever issued it: without it, the report cannot say whose ledger this is.
verify.unavailable: This console has no verifier in the browser. Use the standalone verifier page, or cexchain verify.
verify.verified: Every signature, receipt, and commitment checks, and it comes from the ledger you named.
verify.unconfirmed: Every signature, receipt, and commitment checks. Give the expected ledger id to confirm who issued it.
verify.mismatch: A file is not the one the document committed to.
verify.complete: Complete: the ledger's state proves nothing was left out.
verify.incomplete: The checkpoint cannot prove that nothing, such as a later revocation, was left out.
column.name: Name
approve.name: Name
rules.title: Rules
rules.hint: Rules are the contracts on this ledger: what may happen to a thing, who starts it, and whose consent it needs. The ledger runs them the same way for everyone, and anyone can check that it did.
rules.retire_intro: Retired rules put no new thing under them. Things already under them carry on by the same rules.
rules.retire_reason_hint: Kept on the ledger with the retirement.
rules.read_only: Only an owner or an admin writes rules.
rules.no_compiler: This console was built without the Bo compiler, so it cannot write rules here. Use cexchain bo and cexchain contract deploy.
rules.editor_intro: Fill in the form, or write the Bo text: they are two views of the same rules. Check them, read them as a contract in three languages, run their tests, then deploy them with your passkey.
rules.open_hint: A Bo source (.bo) or a rules sheet (.json), such as one of the examples. A source that fits the form opens in it.
rules.unfit: These rules do not fit the form, so they stay as text: {reason}
rules.source_hint: One clause a line; a block indented by two spaces. Keywords in any of the three languages.
rules.packs_hint: Words for a field of work. A pack's words mean something only when its box is ticked.
rules.explain_hint: Bo wrote these texts from the rules, and each says the same.
rules.no_tests: These rules have no tests yet: add them under Tests in the form.
rules.sheet.contract.hint: The contract's name, such as Lending.
rules.sheet.parties.hint: The roles in these rules, such as owner. Each is a ledger of its own once a thing is created.
rules.sheet.actions.hint: What may happen to the thing, and who starts it.
rules.sheet.rules.hint: What happens by itself when a time comes.
rules.sheet.answers.hint: What happens when a request is done, fails, or expires.
rules.sheet.tests.hint: Each test runs its steps on a thing of its own, every party a ledger of its own.
rules.thing.word.hint: thing, unless a pack you use has a word of its own.
rules.thing.name: Name of the kind
rules.thing.name.hint: Such as Item. Leave it empty for rules without fields.
rules.field.name: Name
rules.field.type.hint: Such as text, number, date, HKD, or a party: the field then holds that party.
rules.action.by.hint: A party, or a field that holds one.
rules.action.to.hint: The other party, such as counterparty.
rules.action.requires.hint: Each must hold, or the call is refused.
rules.action.in_person_over.hint: Such as over 5000: only above it is a person's passkey needed.
rules.action.agents_propose: AI agents may only propose it
rules.input.name: Name
rules.assign.name: Name
rules.rule.when.hint: A time, such as suspended 30 days: a state held that long.
rules.test.name: Name (optional)
rules.test.name.hint: A text in quotes, such as "shared, then closed".
rules.step.args.hint: Such as at 2027-01-05, or in person.
rules.step.expect.hint: Such as a state, consent of friend1, or refused "why".
thing.create_intro: Fill in what the rules ask for. Prepare runs the creation as the ledger will; then your passkey approves it.
thing.what_it_does: What the contract says of it
thing.no_calls: This console cannot show what these rules take: they are not written in Bo, or this console has no compiler.
thing.values_problem: Some values do not fit: see the fields marked.
thing.problem.unknown: The rules take no such value.
thing.problem.literal: Write one value, as in the example.
thing.problem.exact: Finer than its smallest unit, or too large.
thing.problem.ledger: A ledger id is 64 hexadecimal digits.
thing.problem.bound: Too many items for this list.
thing.problem.function: The rules have no such call.
thing.needs_consent: This needs the consent of another ledger ({ledgers}), given on that ledger: ask for it below.
thing.title: A thing under rules
thing.actions_hint: Prepare runs the call as the ledger will and shows what it decides; nothing is signed until your passkey approves it.
thing.requests_hint: Requests the rules made for work outside the ledger. An executor answers them, or you do by hand.
thing.answer_reason_hint: For a failure: a code such as cancelled or unavailable.
thing.share_intro: The proof is a file with every call on this thing: anyone checks it without trusting this console.
exchange.note_hint: Shown to whoever reads the proposal; at most 1000 bytes.
exchange.ask_intro: Write a proposal file and send it to the other party by any channel. They consent on their own ledger and send back a consent file, which you open here to record the call.
exchange.proposal_made: Saved {name}. Send it to the other party; when their consent file comes back, open it from Home.
exchange.title: Proposals and consents
exchange.intro: Open a proposal or consent file someone sent you. It is verified here before you do anything with it.
exchange.verified: Verified: the thing's history checks for the ledger that sent it, and the call is the one it names.
exchange.not_asked: The proposal does not ask this ledger for its consent.
exchange.consent_intro: Your consent names this one call at the thing's current step, and counts once. After the tap, a consent file is saved: send it back.
exchange.consent_made: Saved {name}. Send it back to whoever sent the proposal.
exchange.consent_verified: Verified on the consenting ledger: its terms are this call's.
exchange.not_ours: This consent is to a call on another ledger's thing.
exchange.lapsed: This consent has lapsed: ask again.
exchange.moved_on: The thing has moved on since this consent: ask again.
exchange.record: Record the call with your passkey
exchange.record_intro: The call runs with the consent first, as the ledger will run it.
exchange.link: Open a proposal or consent file
exchange.proposed: This ledger's registrar holds the call until {until}, and records it as soon as the consents come in online.
exchange.no_registrar: This console runs no registrar: ask by file instead.
parties.title: Parties
parties.intro: Other ledgers this console works with: each connected with one code each way. Once connected, calls that wait for your consent on their ledgers show on Home, and your consent goes back online; you ask each other for documents; and each witnesses the other's ledger, cosigning only checkpoints that extend what it cosigned before.
parties.our_fingerprint: This ledger's fingerprint, to compare by voice: {fingerprint}
parties.name: Their name here
parties.name_hint: Letters, digits, dots, dashes, underscores: such as bob.
parties.accept_name_hint: The name you invited them with, if you did.
parties.code_secret: Send it to that party only: it holds the token they call this ledger's API with. Compare fingerprints by voice: {fingerprint}
parties.accepted: Connected with {name}: {organization}, fingerprint {fingerprint}. Compare it with them by voice.
parties.reply_for: Send this code back to {name}, so that they connect with you too:
parties.sent_recorded: Sent to {name}: the call is recorded on their ledger.
parties.sent_waiting: Sent to {name}: the call still waits for other consents.
access.accept_hint: Accepting records a receipt on this ledger and sends it to them.
access.ask_intro: Ask a party reached online for one of its documents. They choose what to share; it comes sealed to this ledger.
access.cannot_grant: You cannot share this document from here: it is not yours to share, or its private data is not here.
access.dismissed: Dismissed: it is no longer asked of you.
access.document_hint: The document's full id, as the party gave it (on a proof they shared, say).
access.fields_hint: Names separated by commas; leave empty to ask for all.
access.grant_days_hint: 1 to 366, and never past the end they asked for.
access.granted_already: You granted this already; granting again replaces the delivery.
access.missing: This document is not on this ledger, or was revoked.
access.not_verified: This delivery does not check out: {message}
access.sent: Sent to {peer}. It shows on Home once they share it.
access.unreadable: This request does not check out: {message}
access.verified: Verified: {by} granted it on {organization}'s ledger, and the document checks against that ledger.
parties.refused: This console refused to cosign {name}'s ledger: {message}. A ledger that does not extend what was cosigned before may have been rewritten, or shown differently to different parties: ask them.
parties.not_cosigned: {name} has not cosigned this ledger's latest checkpoint: {message}
people.title: People
people.intro: Who uses this console, with which role, and what each may do on the ledger. Roles decide what they see and manage here; what they may do on the ledger is a delegation, which the ledger itself checks, always with their passkey's tap.
people.approve_intro: Choose what they may do on the ledger. Then approve, with your passkey: their person on the ledger (with a key this console keeps for them), their passkeys, and what they may do, one tap each.
people.approved: {name} may now act on the ledger, each time with their passkey.
people.until_hint: After this day they may do none of it.
people.may.act: create and act on things under rules
people.may.act_rules: create and act on things under {rules}
people.may.people: register people and grant what they may do
people.withdrawn: Withdrawn: {name} may no longer do it on the ledger.
people.removed: {name} no longer uses this console; withdraw what they may do on the ledger too, if they had anything.
people.link_hint: Send it to them only. It registers a passkey on their own device, once, until {time}; then approve them here.
people.new_key: Their key, kept by this console
tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.intro: For programs that use this ledger's API. A token is shown once, when it is made.
tokens.once: Copy it now: it is not shown again.
activity.title: Activity in this console
thing.action_link_hint: Whoever opens it signs in and sees this action's form; it is checked and approved as any other, so the link holds no secret. Print the code, or show it for a phone to scan.
thing.action_unavailable: The action {action} is not offered on this thing now (or not to you).
automation.title: Automation
automation.intro: Machines act on the ledger without a person's tap: executors answer the requests rules make, AI agents work for a person who answers for them, and the console's own machine fires time rules while the console is unlocked. Each machine may do only what its delegation says.
automation.keeper_runs: The console's machine fires these while the console is unlocked.
automation.keeper_locked: The console is locked: nothing fires until it is unlocked.
automation.executor_intro: An executor answers the requests of some kinds that one set of rules makes (a notice to send, a bill to raise), through its connectors, and may do nothing else. It runs elsewhere, with a key it is given once.
automation.kinds_hint: Separated by commas, as the rules name them: notify, bill.
automation.functions_hint: Leave empty for the rules' own: result, if they have it.
automation.name_hint: Letters, digits, dots, dashes, underscores; it also names its API token.
automation.no_rules: Deploy rules first: an executor answers the requests of a set of rules.
automation.agent_intro: An AI agent works through the MCP server for a person who answers for it. Its statements are a machine's, never in person, and the evidence shows its model.
automation.model_hint: The model it runs, as its maker names it.
automation.no_people: Approve a person first: an AI agent answers to one.
automation.setup_executor: Its key is handed out now, once: the console does not keep it. Choose a passphrase that encrypts it; the executor needs both.
automation.setup_agent: Its key is handed out now, once: the console does not keep it. Choose a passphrase that encrypts it; the MCP server needs both.
automation.passphrase_hint: At least 8 characters. Keep it with the machine, not here.
automation.once: Shown once: save the key and copy the token now.
automation.connectors_hint: Add its connectors to the config first (cexchain executor connector add), and the token to a file.
automation.mcp_hint: Save the token and the passphrase in the files it names, beside the key.
activity.automation.delegate: granted what a machine may do
approve.by_organization: the organization, with its root key: what a machine may do needs no person's presence, so no person's delegation can grant it. This console checks your passkey, and its activity log keeps who approved it.
home.backup_none: No backup yet: the first comes within the day.
home.backup_no_folder: No backup folder: choose one in Settings, and the console backs up every day.
witnesses.title: Public witnesses
witnesses.intro: A public witness cosigns this ledger's checkpoints, so that anyone can tell its history was never rewritten. It learns the ledger's id, its first keys, each checkpoint's size, root, and time, and this computer's address; never statements, records, fields, parties, or files.
witnesses.stopped: {name} is no longer asked. What it cosigned stays valid.
witnesses.key_hint: As its operator publishes it. Check it with them: a witness's own page cannot vouch for itself.
witnesses.add: Ask it to witness this ledger
witnesses.added: {name} cosigned this ledger at {size} entries, and will be asked after each new checkpoint.
activity.witnesses.add: asked a public witness to witness this ledger
relay.title: Reached through a relay
relay.intro: A console on a laptop is reached by its parties through a relay: the server of a public witness it asks. Their requests wait there, sealed for this console, until it fetches and answers them. The relay learns who writes to whom and when, never what.
relay.direct: Parties reach this console directly, at its own address.
relay.used: Parties now reach this console through {name}. Give them a new invitation code.
relay.none_possible: Add a public witness first: its server can be this console's relay.
relay.stopped: Parties reach this console directly again. New invitation codes carry no relay.
relay.problem: The relay could not be reached: {message}
activity.relay.use: chose a relay for parties to reach this console
thing.superseded: A newer version replaced this document (entry {index}). Use the latest version.
register.replaces_hint: This is a new version of {name} ({id}). Once you approve it, anyone who checks the old one is told a newer version replaced it.
search.hint: Searches look at what the ledger holds in the clear: kinds, states, times, and public information. Private fields are never searched; they stay sealed.
report.title: Reports
report.hint: Counts of what the ledger holds, from its search index. Days are in this browser's time ({offset}).
report.unavailable: This console's node keeps no search index, so it has no reports.
report.sum_hint: The field's name in the rules, such as total or fee.
report.truncated: Only the first 10,000 groups are shown.
